title: default value masks a failed lookup
question: Does a ?? or || default here substitute for a lookup that should have succeeded, so a missing definition, item or pawn becomes a plausible-looking zero, empty array or false instead of an error the caller can see?
fail_requires: what the lookup was supposed to return
the observable symptom in the sim when it misses (a pawn idling, an order never completing, a stat reading zero)
not_a_finding: a default for a genuinely optional field
a default on a value the caller checks immediately afterwards

title: caught error is discarded
question: Does a catch block here discard the error without logging it, rethrowing, or putting the caller into a state that reflects the failure?
fail_requires: what can throw inside the try
what the caller believes happened afterwards
not_a_finding: a catch that logs through the project's gated logger
a catch around a genuinely optional probe (feature detection, an optional file read) whose failure is the expected branch

title: early return leaves the caller with no signal
question: Does this symbol return early on a precondition failure without telling the caller anything — no return value distinction, no state change, no log — so the caller cannot distinguish 'did the work' from 'declined to'?
fail_requires: the caller that cannot tell the difference
not_a_finding: a guard whose caller re-checks the same condition
a void tick handler where declining to act is the normal per-tick outcome
a return whose value already encodes the decline
